facts.text: Chodov joined the Prague municipality in 1968, shifting from a separate village to an urban district.
The C‑line metro station in Chodov opened in 1998, making the area one of the newest stops in Prague’s underground network.
In 1999 the National Archives moved into a striking modern building inside Westfield Chodov, the shopping centre that sits above the metro station.
Westfield Chodov is one of the largest shopping malls in the Czech Republic, boasting more than 210 stores and a wide range of services.
After the Velvet Revolution, Chodov’s skyline changed from mainly high‑rise post‑war housing to a mix of commercial sites and detached homes.
Geographically, Chodov lies in the southeast part of Prague, offering a suburban feel while remaining well connected to the city centre.
